metadata.file_name: Brit J of Edu Psychol - 2023 - Qin - Learning strategies and reading achievement in primary schools  Longitudinal.pdf
metadata.title: Learning strategies and reading achievement in primary schools: Longitudinal relationship and gender differences

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a two-wave longitudinal sample of Chinese primary students in Grade 4 (T1) and Grade 6 (T2) drawn from 99 schools, with whole-class sampling (one or two classes per school) and stratification of schools by location (city/town/rural). The manuscript does not report the use of any complex survey weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures; analyses were conducted in Mplus using a robust maximum likelihood estimator and a hierarchical-data option (type=complex) to account for clustering. Missingness at T2 was handled via full information maximum likelihood (FIML) rather than by listwise deletion, and the final analytic sample comprised 3878 students after attrition. Because no ILSA sampling weights are documented, results should be interpreted as model-based estimates for the sampled schools/classes rather than population-representative estimates for all of China.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable (reading achievement) was estimated using Rasch linking and Expected a Posterior Estimation (EAP) from a self-developed test, and the longitudinal relationships were estimated with cross-lagged structural equation modeling in Mplus. Plausible Values (PV) are not used in this study because the outcome is not an ILSA PV-based achievement scale; instead, it is an EAP score on a Rasch-linked test. Missing data were handled using full information maximum likelihood (FIML), which is treated here as a form of model-based imputation under the provided schema mapping.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were surveyed at two time points: Grade 4 (T1) and Grade 6 (T2). At T1, 3886 students from 99 schools in four Chinese provinces participated using whole-class sampling (one or two classes sampled per school), with schools stratified by location (city/town/rural). At T2, 1163 students withdrew; 447 were absent because they were moved to other larger schools and could not be tracked, while remaining attrition was due to illness, unwillingness, or transfers to different classes/schools. The final analytic sample contained 3878 students with complete gender information (8 students with missing gender were excluded). Reading achievement was assessed within 40 minutes and questionnaire completion averaged 15 minutes; the analysis used mean strategy scores at T1 and T2 and controlled for gender, age, and parents’ educational levels.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2009 (adapted learning strategies), China Grade 4→Grade 6 reading achievement (self-developed test)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Cross-lagged model (Mplus) fit: χ2(14)=102.739, CFI=0.992, TLI=0.965, RMSEA=0.040 (90% CI: .033–.048), SRMR=0.027. Significant path: prior memorization → subsequent reading achievement (β=0.138, p<.001). Prior reading achievement → subsequent strategies (β=0.223, p<.001 for memorization; β=0.187, p<.001 for elaboration; β=0.192, p<.001 for control). Prior elaboration/control → subsequent reading achievement: not reported as significant (described as only memorization predicting reading).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2009-adapted learning strategies and China Grade 4→Grade 6 longitudinal data with reading achievement measured on a self-developed Rasch-linked test, the study leveraged memorization strategy at T1 (and controlled for gender, age, and parents’ education) to predict subsequent reading achievement at T2, finding that only prior memorization significantly predicted later reading achievement (β=0.138, p<.001), while prior elaboration and control did not. This indicates that strengthening memorization practices that support deep processing may be more effective for improving reading achievement in early primary grades, though the design is correlational and cannot establish causal effects.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2009 (adapted learning strategies), China Grade 4→Grade 6 longitudinal data
main_findings.performance_metrics: Significant paths: prior reading achievement → subsequent control (β=0.192, p<.001). Prior memorization → subsequent control (β=0.159, p<.001). Prior elaboration → subsequent control (β=0.100, p<.001). Prior control → subsequent memorization/elaboration: not significant (β=0.004, p>0.05 for control→memorization; β=0.006, p>0.05 for control→elaboration).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2009-adapted learning strategies and China Grade 4→Grade 6 longitudinal the study leveraged prior reading achievement and lower-level strategies (memorization and elaboration) to predict subsequent control strategies at T2, finding that prior reading achievement and both memorization and elaboration significantly predicted later control (β=0.192, p<.001; β=0.159, p<.001; β=0.100, p<.001), while prior control did not predict later memorization or elaboration. This indicates that in primary reading development, lower-level strategy use and achievement may function as precursors for later metacognitive/control strategy development, suggesting that instruction should scaffold from memorization/elaboration toward control rather than expecting control to drive earlier strategy adoption.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2009 (adapted learning strategies), China Grade 4→Grade 6 longitudinal data (multigroup by gender)
main_findings.target_variable: Gender moderation of prior reading achievement → later strategies
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multigroup cross-lagged model fit: χ2(22)=110.644, CFI=0.992, TLI=0.962, RMSEA=0.046 (90% CI: .037–.054), SRMR=0.031. Nested model tests: significant gender differences for paths from prior reading achievement to later memorization (Δχ2(1)=3.754, p<.05), elaboration (Δχ2(1)=5.898, p<.05), and control (Δχ2(1)=7.198, p<.01). Final model: boys showed stronger effects from prior reading achievement on later strategies (β=0.246/0.214/0.224) than girls (β=0.191/0.151/0.151) for memorization/elaboration/control respectively.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2009-adapted learning strategies and China Grade 4→Grade 6 multigroup longitudinal modeling, the study leveraged prior reading achievement and gender to test whether the achievement-to-strategy relationship differed by boys versus girls, finding that the effects of prior reading achievement on later memorization, elaboration, and control were significantly stronger for boys than for girls (with significant Δχ2 tests and larger standardized paths for boys). This indicates that boys may be more responsive to prior achievement signals when adopting subsequent learning strategies, suggesting that gender-responsive feedback and scaffolding that links strategy use to performance may help narrow reading achievement gaps.

data.outcome_summary: This longitudinal study followed Chinese primary students across two waves (Grade 4 to Grade 6), measuring reading achievement with a self-developed 33-item multiple-choice test linked across waves using a Rasch model and scored via EAP, and measuring learning strategies (memorization, elaboration, control) using scales adapted from PISA 2009. The analytic sample included 3878 students from 99 schools in four provinces, with attrition at T2 handled using full information maximum likelihood (FIML) and clustering accounted for in Mplus via the type=complex option. The cross-lagged model fit well (e.g., χ2(14)=102.739, CFI=0.992, RMSEA=0.040), and the key predictive pattern was that only prior memorization significantly predicted later reading achievement (β=0.138, p<.001), while prior reading achievement predicted later strategies. Gender moderation tests showed stronger achievement-to-strategy effects for boys than girls. Limitations include the absence of PV-based ILSA achievement modeling and the correlational nature of cross-lagged paths, so causal claims cannot be made.
